items.title: AMA: physicians shouldn’t be the last line of defense against clinical AI harm
items.summary: The AMA argues doctors can’t be held responsible for harm when much of AI development and deployment is outside their control.

items.title: Treat AI chatbots as shared decision-making aids, not oracles
items.summary: Framing chatbots as support for patient-clinician conversations can help engagement while limiting risk.

items.title: Doximity’s dose-verification tool beats general-purpose AI models
items.summary: Company research claims its clinical AI outperformed general models as large AI labs enter healthcare.

items.title: 91% of patients want to approve AI use in diagnosis; 64% of providers plan AI for claims and denials
items.summary: Survey figures from the weekly roundup show a gap between patient consent expectations and provider revenue-cycle plans.
